NKJV renders the phrase glossed “wearied with weariness” as “being caused to fly swiftly”; the meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.

Close to the Hebrew; “a word went forth” is rendered “the command went out,” and “you are precious” “you are greatly beloved.”

NKJV renders “seventy sevens” as “Seventy weeks,” “to complete sin” as “To make an end of sins,” “to atone” as “To make reconciliation,” “prophet” as “prophecy,” and “a holy of holies” as “the Most Holy.”
NKJV renders “an anointed one, a prince” as “Messiah the Prince,” “sevens” as “weeks,” and “a plaza and a moat” as “The street … and the wall.”
NKJV renders “an anointed one will be cut off and will have nothing” as “Messiah shall be cut off, but not for Himself.”
Close to the Hebrew; “one seven” is rendered “one week,” and NKJV supplies “shall be one who makes desolate” for “on a wing of abominations, desolating.”
